title: The Leeward Current
premise: Beatrix Whitlock, a desert ranger with a compass that belonged to the sister who died on the Leeward Glacier nine years ago, is hired by her old rival Cassian Voss to escort an expedition back across the ice before the calving season seals the route. The crew believes they are retrieving scientific instruments, but Voss is actually hunting the wreck of the first expedition — the one Beatrix's sister died on and the one Voss swore off after a betrayal he has never explained. What they find in the ice forces Beatrix to choose between the loyalty that has defined her and a truth that would destroy the legend her sister's memory rests on. She brings the crew home through the calving route with the evidence, but chooses to bury the truth with her sister, keeping only the compass — and a debt finally paid.
about_author: Emrys Sandoval is a former expedition cook who spent six seasons in high-altitude base camps before turning to fiction, claiming the best stories were always told over rehydrated dinners. The Leeward Current is a fourth novel, written largely in notebooks that survived two river crossings and one avalanche.

chapters.title: Salt on the Wind
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Tracking a petty thief across the salt flats, Beatrix catches him but lets him go when he mentions a compass like hers. The emotional beat is restlessness — a life of small pursuits that no longer add up to anything.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Back in the frontier town of Corren's Rest, Beatrix reviews her accounts: money owed, favors spent, the anniversary of her sister Wren's death approaching. A letter arrives with no signature, only a glacier map and a date. Beat: dread dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: An Old Rival's Terms
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Cassian Voss, older and grayer than the man who ruined her reputation years ago, offers a contract: guide his crew to the Leeward Glacier and back before calving season. He refuses to say what they're retrieving. Beat: pride wrestling with need.

chapters.title: The Crew Assembles
chapters.summary: POV Odile, the expedition's cartographer. She assembles the team — a disgraced glaciologist, a mute mechanic named Ferro, and a young porter, Tam, eager and untested. Odile suspects Voss is hiding something but needs the money. Beat: wary camaraderie forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Departure at First Light
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The crew leaves Corren's Rest. Beatrix tests Voss's story and finds it holds — barely. Tam asks about her compass; she deflects. Beat: the last easy day, tension humming beneath banter.

chapters.title: The Threshold of Green
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The desert gives way to scrubland and then the first glaciers' foothills. Ferro's repaired engine fails on a river crossing; Beatrix's quick thinking saves the supplies and earns grudging respect. Beat: the team becoming a team.

chapters.title: What the Porter Saw
chapters.summary: POV Tam. On night watch, Tam sees Voss burning papers and hears him say Wren's name. He tells Beatrix, who goes cold — Voss was on the first expedition. Beat: betrayal surfacing, trust cracking.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Confronting Voss at dawn, she extracts a partial truth: the first expedition found something in the ice, Wren died securing it, and Voss swore the route sealed forever. He won't say what it was. Beat: grief and anger braided together.

chapters.title: The White Corridor
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The crew enters the glacier valley. Crevasses, whiteout, and Odile's maps — drawn partly from Wren's recovered notes — keep them alive. Beat: awe and terror in equal measure; the mountain as antagonist.

chapters.title: Wren's Cache
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. They reach a cairn Wren built before she died. Inside: her journal, half-fused in ice. Beatrix reads the first pages alone and learns the expedition found a ship — a vessel frozen in the glacier centuries old. Beat: the past becoming unbearably present.

chapters.title: The Thing in the Ice
chapters.summary: POV Tam. The crew reaches the wreck: a sailing ship embedded in blue ice, impossibly far inland. Tam's wonder curdles when they realize the hull is scorched from the inside. Beat: discovery tipping into unease.

chapters.title: Voss's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Voss finally tells all: the first crew burned the ship's cargo rather than let it reach civilization; Wren died doing it; the sworn-off job was to make sure it stayed buried. Someone in his crew was paid to reopen the wound. Beat: truth arriving too heavy to set down.

chapters.title: The Fifth Man
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile deduces the glaciologist, Merrick, has been transmitting their position. Confronted, he admits a collector hired him — the same buyer who funded the original expedition. Beat: paranoia; the enemy was inside all along.

chapters.title: Stormlock
chapters.summary: POV Tam. A katabatic storm pins the crew at the wreck for three days. Supplies dwindle; Merrick sabotages the radio. Tam and Ferro improvise a repair. Beat: endurance, and Tam growing into someone the others rely on.

chapters.title: Merrick's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Merrick offers Beatrix the buyer's price — enough to erase every debt — for safe passage out with a sample of the cargo. She refuses, but the offer plants the question the whole book has been building: what is loyalty worth? Beat: temptation made flesh.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Route
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The calving season opens early. The glacier begins to shed; the return corridor is collapsing day by day. Odile charts a desperate alternate route through the icefall — the one Wren's journal marks in red. Beat: the clock now audible in every scene.

chapters.title: Merrick Runs
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Merrick steals supplies and a sledge and strikes out alone across the icefall. Tam follows against orders and finds him dead in a crevasse field, the sample vials shattered in his frozen hand. Beat: the cost of betrayal, pitiable even in victory.

chapters.title: The Icefall Crossing
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The crew crosses Wren's red route as the glacier groans apart around them. Beatrix nearly loses the compass — and with it her nerve — but Ferro pulls her back. Beat: the physical climax; survival earned inch by inch.

chapters.title: What We Carry Out
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. On the far side, the crew takes stock: Voss's evidence of the first expedition's fate, Wren's journal, and the decision of what to tell the world. Voss argues for silence; Odile argues for the record. Beat: the moral climax, arguments that cost friendships.

chapters.title: The Choice at Corren's Rest
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Back in town, the buyer's agents wait with contracts and threats. Beatrix reads Wren's final journal page aloud to the crew — Wren chose silence to protect people who would never know her name. Beatrix chooses the same. Beat: loyalty and truth reconciled at last.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The expedition dissolves quietly: Voss pays everyone and vanishes, Ferro takes work on the coast, Tam signs on to Odile's next survey. Odile files a report that says only 'route impassable, nothing found.' Beat: bittersweet peace, secrets kept as a kind of gift.

chapters.title: The Leeward Current
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. A year later, Beatrix returns to the salt flats, no longer hunting anything. She sets the compass on Wren's cairn at the glacier's edge — the needle still pointing leeward, toward the buried ship and the sister who stayed with it. Beat: release; identity no longer defined by debt.
